newsitem.title: USA: Ranson Capital Corp plans Illinois muni bond fund.
newsitem.headline: Ranson Capital Corp plans Illinois muni bond fund.

text.p: Ranson Capital Corp, a subsidiary of ND Holdings Inc, announced Wednesday it plans to launch as early as mid-October a municipal bond fund specializing in Illinois debt.

Ranson's would be the first mutual fund devoted to Illinois municipal securities and would continue the company's focus on the smaller investor, said Patrick Schmidt, compliance coordinator for ND Holdings.
Ranson filed its application for the fund with the Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this week, Schmidt said.

Most bonds issued by Illinois state and local governments hold no state tax exemption, but Ranson believes the fund will still be attractive to investors, Schmidt said. It could also include some bonds exempt from Illinois income taxes, such as those issued by commonwealths, he added.
"A lot of people want to keep their money invested in their home state," Schmidt said.
The fund will allow those who already invest in Illinois debt to diversify their holdings and begin investments at a minimum of $1,000, Schmidt said.
Sales charges of 4.25 percent apply to investments and earnings can be distributed monthly or reinvested.

ND Holdings has tax-exempt municipal bond funds for North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, Kansas, Nebraska and Oklahoma, as well as the Integrity Fund of Funds, which invests in leading stock mutual funds.
